title: Revenue tile shows Parts and Labor as whole percentages, or the invoice count
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  1. User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. Location: you are in a fresh test location made for this run, so nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  3. Timing: you run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  4. Data: a test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101). Its Default Shop Supplies is 0, so the invoice carries only labor and parts.
  5. Data: an in-stock inventory part with a Sell price (e.g. $100.00) that this location can sell.
  6. People (Advisor A): you (Admin ShopView); the Service Advisor in the work order's left panel shows your name by default.
  7. Data: one work order for that customer, ready but not invoiced yet: Service Advisor Advisor A, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour (Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00) with the part added (quantity 1, In stock); line completed and the work order marked reviewed.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Revenue tile's range pill to This Week and read the line under the amount.
  2. Click Work Orders, open the prepared work order, click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice. Close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying.
  3. On the invoice write down the labor total and the parts total (e.g. Labor $200.00 = 2.00 hours x $100.00, Parts $100.00). If the invoice also shows shop supplies, write that amount down too.
  4. Work out the split by hand: Parts = $100.00 / ($100.00 + $200.00) x 100 = 33.33, shown as 33. Labor = $200.00 / $300.00 x 100 = 66.67, shown as 67.
  5. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week again and read the line under the amount.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: Before the invoice: Revenue reads $0.00 and the line under it reads "0 Invoices", because there is no parts-and-labor split to show.
  • Step 5: After the invoice: the line reads "Parts 33% · Labor 67%", each a whole number (33.33 rounds to 33, 66.67 rounds to 67), and the two add up to 100. There is no "Other" share, because the invoice has no shop supplies or fees.
  • Step 3: If the invoice shows shop supplies or a fee, the customer's Default Shop Supplies is not 0: mark this test Blocked: "setup not done" and write the amounts in the comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v50 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 16 Oct 2026, S4 (S4-R3, S4-N2), S3 (S3-E3, Revenue split sentence). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; screenshots of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After ("Parts 39% · Labor 61%"), 15_Empty_After ("0 Invoices").

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}% · Other {other}%", each percent a whole number of the tile’s revenue. Parts is parts sales, net of credits (as today). Labor is labor sales only, the same figure as the Sales report’s Labor column. Other is everything else in revenue: shop supplies, fees and any other line that is neither a part nor labor. The three are rounded so they always add up to 100. "· Other {other}%" is left off when Other rounds to 0%, so a shop with no supplies or fees reads "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%".”
  • S4-N2: “If the Revenue tile has no parts-versus-labor split to show, its supporting line reads "{count} Invoices" instead.”
  • S3-E3 (Revenue split sentence): “The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026, before the expected results changed on 16 Oct 2026; the changed results have not yet been checked against a build.
